correctness.rationale: Saliola's path algebra theorem applies over every field. Each arrow lowers subset size by at least two. The only internal vertices have size 2 or 3, ten of each; they have incoming/outgoing multiplicities (5,1) or (1,5), and cannot be joined to each other. Each of the 100 length-two paths belongs to one internal vertex, the arrow sets of these blocks are disjoint, and the other 74 of the 194 arrows annihilate the radical. The 20 direct summands consist of B and its opposite, and polynomial group inversion sends the opposite factor to the same group functor over every test ring. The commutator ab′−a′b has common kernel zero on the noncentral coordinates (take b′=1 and arbitrary a′), giving center dimension 174 and class two. In one factor the commutator rank is 0, 1 or 5, and dividing the corresponding element counts by q to that rank gives the three class coefficients. For commuting tuples either the b-vector is zero or aᵢ=v bᵢ for a unique v; multiplying by freely chosen central coordinates and taking the product gives the displayed all-s formula. The exponent support is the union of integer intervals [5b,20+4b], b=0,…,20, leaving precisely the stated six holes; evaluation at T=1 gives the stated total. Independent replay, python3 /workspace/frozen_math_replay.py 5, reconstructs composable pairs literally and verifies the disjoint blocks and exponent set; the all-field and all-arity assertions follow from the argument, not the finite replay.
residual_risks: These counts concern 1+J only, not the full unit group.

evidence: Saliola gives the subset-quiver and its path-algebra realization. Hennecart–Perry's source/sink splits preserve the radical: separate sources by their internal targets and sinks by their internal origins, and isolate arrows directly from a source to a sink. In this quiver each two-path vertex is size 2 or 3, so the resulting connected pieces are the ten (5,1) and ten (1,5) stars and 74 single arrows. Their Proposition 4.1 also gives the commuting-pair count per three-vertex radical with these dimensions. Rossmann's Theorem A gives ordinary size distributions generally for graphical groups.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general short-quiver splitting and subset arrow multiplicities supply the group product; the complete size enumerator is then the already evaluated graphical-star polynomial, not a new class calculation requiring analysis in the full five-generator algebra.
searches: arXiv:2208.07738v1, Theorems 3.12 and 3.18, Corollary 3.19 and Proposition 4.1

evidence: For a noncentral star element with b=0, its centralizer consists of b′=0 and is abelian; with b≠0 it consists of a′=(a/b)b′ and is again abelian. The known star class-size polynomial gives the numbers of elements in centralizer orders q¹⁰ and q⁶ as q⁵(q⁵−1) and q¹⁰(q−1), and the center has order q⁵.

Grouping commuting tuples by the first element, the standard centralizer recurrence is tₛ=q⁵tₛ₋₁+q⁵(q⁵−1)q^[10(s−1)]+q¹⁰(q−1)q^[6(s−1)], with t₀=1. Its solution is tₛ=q^(5s)[q^(5s)+q⁵(qˢ−1)], and direct products give q^(74s)tₛ²⁰.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The pair-count result in isolation does not imply all arities or class-size multiplicities. The decisive combination is the stronger published graphical-star size distribution, the immediate abelianness of its noncentral centralizers, and the standard centralizer recurrence. Beyond those implications, the six holes follow by taking the support of a polynomial product with positive coefficients.

evidence: The star group presentation has five leaf generators and one hub generator with central commutators along the five edges. These are exactly the a, b and z coordinates of H₅: map leaf i at r to (r eᵢ,0,0), the hub at r to (0,r,0), and the i-th edge coordinate at r to (0,0,r eᵢ), choosing the commutator sign by vertex ordering. Ordered leaf/hub/edge factors give unique coordinates over every commutative ring.
Example 5.4 states X^(n−1)[(X²−X)Yⁿ+(Xⁿ−1)Y+X]. At n=5 this is q⁵+q⁴(q⁵−1)T+q⁵(q−1)T⁵.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The identification is an actual group isomorphism in all characteristics, not just equality of commutator ranks or a similar title. Conjugacy classes multiply over direct products and each element of the central additive factor contributes a singleton.

originality.rationale: The main size polynomial is an exact prior specialization beyond the frozen record's pair-count comparison. The local rectangular group H₅ is Rossmann's graphical group of the star K₅,₁ as a group functor; Example 5.4 explicitly evaluates its entire ordinary class-size polynomial over every finite field. Saliola's subset quiver and the radical-preserving source/sink decomposition mechanically give 20 such factors and 74 additive factors by subset-size bookkeeping. The six missing exponents are the support of the resulting product. Higher arities are also mechanically determined in this case, not by the pair total alone: all noncentral centralizers of a star factor are abelian, so the standard all-arity centralizer recurrence applied to the known star size polynomial yields the displayed formula. No claim is made that the prior papers print the five-generator formula verbatim.
residual_risks: Whether the exact five-letter specialization was written out verbatim elsewhere is unresolved; the failure is based on demonstrated implications, not on a search miss.
